summary: Practise QGIS mapping, vulnerability analysis and coverage monitoring for social protection and humanitarian targeting. Explore the course.
lede: Geospatial targeting and decision support links location data to vulnerability, geographic equity and programme coverage in social protection and humanitarian programmes. It helps GIS specialists, programme managers and MEAL teams prepare and join spatial data in QGIS, compare vulnerability indicators, review targeting boundaries and assess coverage. Practical exercises also address data quality, uncertainty and the limits of satellite and population data when producing operational map summaries.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who use spatial evidence to select, reach or monitor households and communities in social protection and humanitarian programmes.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with GIS layers, attribute tables and basic spatial concepts is recommended. No programming is required. Bring a laptop with QGIS installed for hands-on exercises.
